findings.title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this check is false for production workers and a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts. The old and replacement workers can then flush the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate production and accumulating stuck processes. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from processes instead.

findings.title: Terminate remaining workers even after the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks before cleaning up the remaining workers. If the first worker consumes the timeout, all later workers are left running, potentially blocked in Redis or Kafka calls despite the stopped flag. During rebalancing the new strategy can start replacement flushers while these old workers still own the same shards. The deadline should limit waiting, not skip termination of the remaining processes.
